bib.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition

question: How does convolutional network depth affect accuracy in large-scale image recognition when all other design choices are fixed and 3x3 filters are used throughout?
hypothesis: Increasing depth with very small 3x3 filters improves accuracy over prior-art configurations.
contributions: Thorough evaluation of networks of increasing depth (11 to 19 weight layers) with 3x3 filters
Features generalise to other datasets with state-of-the-art results
Two best models (D, E) publicly released

method.summary: Six ConvNet configurations (A-E, plus A-LRN) differing only in depth (11-19 weight layers), all 3x3 convs (config C adds 1x1), trained on ILSVRC-2012 with SGD, scale jittering, and evaluated densely, multi-scale, multi-crop and as ensembles. Models also used as frozen feature extractors with linear SVM, and for localisation.
method.task: image classification (ILSVRC-2012), localisation, transfer feature extraction

datasets.name: ILSVRC-2012
datasets.split: most experiments evaluated on val as test; some on test via official server
datasets.preprocessing: subtract training-set mean RGB; random 224x224 crop from isotropically rescaled image, random horizontal flip, random RGB colour shift

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC-2007/2012 classification
datasets.split: official train/val/test; VOC-2012 test via server
datasets.preprocessing: features L2-normalised, averaged over scales Q in {256,384,512,640,768}

datasets.name: Caltech-101
datasets.split: 3 random splits, 30 train and up to 50 test images per class, 20% of train as validation

datasets.name: Caltech-256
datasets.split: 3 random splits, 60 train images per class, rest test, 20% of train as validation

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC-2012 action classification
datasets.preprocessing: features on whole image, optionally stacked with person bounding-box features

models.name: VGG A (11 layers)
models.hidden: conv width starts at 64 and doubles after each max-pool up to 512; FC 4096 x2 then 1000

models.name: VGG B (13)
models.init_from: first 4 conv and last 3 FC from net A, rest random

training.objective: multinomial logistic regression (softmax cross-entropy); Euclidean loss for localisation
training.lr: 10^-2 initially (10^-3 for S=384 initialised from S=256, and for localisation)
training.lr_schedule: divided by 10 when validation accuracy stopped improving; decreased 3 times
training.dropout: 0.5 on the first two FC layers
training.regularisation: weight decay, dropout, scale jittering S in [256;512], flips, RGB colour shift
training.hardware: 4x NVIDIA Titan Black GPUs, synchronous data parallelism

other.multi_scale_training: fine-tune all layers of single-scale model pre-trained at S=384; for the submission only the FC layers of D were fine-tuned
other.implementation: derived from C++ Caffe (Dec 2013 branch), multi-GPU, full-size multi-scale
other.init_note: after submission found Glorot & Bengio (2010) init works without pre-training
other.preinit_layers_lr: learning rate not reduced for pre-initialised layers

inference.decoding: dense fully-convolutional application (FC->7x7 conv and 1x1 convs), spatial average of class score map, average with horizontal flip
inference.samples: deterministic; no seeds or repeated runs reported

parameters.test_scale_Q: Q=S for fixed S; Q=0.5(Smin+Smax) for jittered single-scale; multi-scale Q={S-32,S,S+32} or {256,384,512}
parameters.multi_crop: 50 crops per scale (5x5 grid x 2 flips), 150 crops over 3 scales

metrics.name: top-5 error
metrics.definition: proportion of images whose ground-truth class is outside the top-5 predictions

metrics.name: localisation error
metrics.definition: top-5 error with box correct if IoU > 0.5

metrics.name: mAP / mean class recall
metrics.definition: VOC mean average precision; Caltech mean class recall

eval.protocol: single run per config; validation set used as test for most; ILSVRC test via official server; Caltech 3 random splits with mean +- std; no significance tests

availability.code: models released at http://www.robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/very_deep/ (D and E); training code not stated

evidence.quote: the L2 penalty multiplier set to 5·10−4

limits: Error saturates at 19 layers on ImageNet; authors say deeper may help on larger datasets but do not test it
Single runs, no seeds or variance for ILSVRC results
Initialisation from shallow net A was needed to train deeper nets; the authors later found Glorot init removes this
Multi-crop vs dense gain attributed to boundary conditions only as a hypothesis
Localisation did not use scale jittering or OverFeat's resolution enhancement
Parameter count (~140M, mostly in FC layers) and 2-3 weeks of training on 4 GPUs; superseded by residual networks (not in this paper)
Several VOC comparisons are against methods using extended pre-training sets
